paper.title_en: Impact of Einstein–Euler–Heisenberg nonlinear electrodynamic on strong-gravitational field instabilities and chaotic dynamics in Kerr black holes
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the emergence of strong-gravity chaos in rotating black holes (BHs) within the framework of Einstein–Euler–Heisenberg nonlinear electrodynamic (EEH-NLED) gravity. We derive the equations of motion for null geodesics and analyze circular photon orbits together with their stability using Lyapunov exponents. The phase-space structure of photon dynamics is examined through Poincaré sections, revealing the onset of chaotic behavior in the strong field regime. The chaotic behavior is quantitatively characterized using several complementary indicators, including the largest Lyapunov exponent (LLE), the Fast Lyapunov Indicator (FLI) and Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. We show that the strictly positive Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy associated with photon trajectories in EEH-NLED gravity constitutes a clear and quantitative indicator of chaotic dynamics and an inherent instability of the underlying spacetime geometry. These findings further substantiate the robustness of Hawking radiation with respect to NLED effects and quantum-gravity induced corrections. Our results show that NLED corrections significantly alter the geodesic dynamics and can induce pronounced chaotic features in rotating BH spacetimes. These findings underscore the importance of NLED effects in shaping photon motion near BHs and provide new insights into the interplay between strong gravity and chaos, with potential implications for BH shadows, namely the dark silhouette determined by unstable photon trajectories, and related observational signatures. •We examine the impact of Einstein–Euler–Heisenberg nonlinear electrodynamics on strong-gravity instabilities and on the emergence of chaotic dynamics in Kerr black hole spacetimes.•The stability properties of null circular geodesics are quantified via the computation of the maximal Lyapunov exponent.•Chaotic trajectories are investigated by means of Poincar sections, the Kolmogorov Sinai entropy, and the Weighted Birkhoff average.•The results indicate that electromagnetic fields substantially influence the structure of phase space and the resulting particle dynamics in the vicinity of rotating black holes.
